title: 1960 AHSME Problem 7

concepts.label: Power scaling of length, area, and volume

statement: Circle I passes through the center of, and is tangent to, circle II. The area of circle I is \(4\) square inches. Then the area of circle II, in square inches, is:

solutions.text:
Because circle I passes through the center of circle II, the distance between the centers equals the radius \(r\) of circle I. Internal tangency also makes that distance \(R-r,\) where \(R\) is the radius of circle II. Thus \(R=2r,\) and the area is multiplied by \(2^2=4.\) It is therefore \(4\cdot4=16.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Draw the line through the two centers and the tangency point
The radius of circle II is twice the radius of circle I
